name: AIDA
blueprintProse:
The AIDA framework allocates structural weight across four sequential phases designed to progress a prospect from passive observation to active transactional commitment. The Attention component commands roughly 15% of the total word count, utilizing unexpected assertions or jarring telemetry to break reader habituation. The Interest component consumes 30% of the budget, contextualizing why the status quo has fractured and building mechanistic curiosity. The Desire phase occupies the largest allocation at 40%, grounding technical capabilities into concrete business outcomes and social validation. The final Action phase represents 15% of the copy, providing an unambiguous, low-friction command specifying the immediate next step. 
The psychological power of AIDA rests upon the orienting reflex and narrative transportation. The human central nervous system filters out routine stimuli through sensory gating, responding only when an external input deviates from expected patterns. Once the orienting reflex interrupts passive skimming, the interest and desire segments trigger narrative transportation, enabling the reader to mentally simulate the operational relief of adopting the proposed mechanism before committing to the final action.
